subject: astronomy
title: Active Galactic Nuclei: Quasars and Seyferts
welcome_lead: Galaxies whose cores outshine the rest of the galaxy.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: quasars, blazars and Seyfert galaxies.
final_note: AGN are powered by supermassive black holes.

concepts.def: Active Galactic Nucleus — bright, compact central engine.
AGN whose jet points nearly at Earth.
Nearby spiral with a bright, broad-line nucleus.
Collimated outflow of relativistic plasma from an AGN.
Different AGN types are the same engine viewed at different angles.

walkthroughs.body_html: Quasars are the most luminous AGN, often outshining their host galaxies. The first identified quasar, 3C 273 (1963), is still one of the brightest. Most are at high redshift.
Seyfert galaxies, named after Carl Seyfert (1943), are nearer and lower luminosity, with bright nuclei and broad emission lines. Type 1 shows broad lines; Type 2 shows narrow.
The unification model says quasars, Seyferts and blazars are the same kind of engine — supermassive black hole plus accretion disk plus jet — seen at different angles relative to the dusty torus.
